📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

Sources indicate that the stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

It's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

Recent findings suggest that also, in True Detective, Daddario's character, Lisa, refuses to be disregarded while serving as a mistress to Detective Hart. So, with these two HBO roles alone, I believe Daddario can give both sensuality and substance while playing a Bond Girl. I also want to see her chemistry with Robert Pattinson. While the two have never done a project together, I can see them playing off each other well.

While we don’t know yet who will be the lucky lady to play the next Bond Girl, I'm keeping my fingers crossed for Alexandra Daddario to get the part. Hopefully, additional information on the upcoming film -- which is being directed by Denis Villeneuve -- will arrive sooner rather than later. In the meantime, though, you can watch Daddario in the 2026 movie release Hershey, which is in theaters now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

"Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

It's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another firm's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

Sources indicate that "Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

It has been revealed that devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

Recent findings suggest that for the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a manufacturer mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

Devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its strategy with each fresh GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

"On November 12th, our board of directors revealed that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the firm's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). Industry observers note that "Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

#63154. How to Make Sure an 'Onion' Site on the Dark Web Is Legitimate

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1018 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

How to Make Sure an 'Onion' Site on the Dark Web Is Legitimate

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1018 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the dark web isn't just for illicit activities.
  • According to recent reports, but this also provides perfect cover for criminals and hackers who create clones of legitimate dark web sites to steal sensitive data and cryptocurrency from privacy-conscious users.
  • Thankfully, Tor Browser already has a cryptography-backed feature that can verify the authenticity of an onion site, by confirming whether it has end-to-end encryption and extended validation certificates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the dark web isn't just for illicit activities. In fact, many legitimate online platforms maintain a ".onion" domain on the dark web for privacy reasons, including media outlets like ProPublica and BBC News, social media sites like Facebook, and privacy-conscious communication platforms like Proton Mail and SecureDrop.

According to recent reports, but this also provides perfect cover for criminals and hackers who create clones of legitimate dark web sites to steal sensitive data and cryptocurrency from privacy-conscious users. And given that onion links are long and jumbled, it’s easy for users to accidentally click on the wrong link and end up on a fake website instead of the real one. When the FBI seized 276 onion addresses during 2014's Operation Onymous, they found that 153 of them were phishing sites.

Thankfully, Tor Browser already has a cryptography-backed feature that can verify the authenticity of an onion site, by confirming whether it has end-to-end encryption and extended validation certificates. Here's how this feature works, where it falters, as well as what other red flags you should look for.

According to recent reports, while phishing on the dark web works as it does on the clear web, scammers have a few unique advantages due to the secretive nature of the environment. Most importantly, you can’t just glance at an onion link to tell if the site is genuine. Normal website URLs tend to be short and memorable, while onion links are 56-character strings of alphanumeric text that look mostly like gibberish.

When you try to connect, Tor Browser verifies the URL against the originating website’s cryptographic key, which is how you know nobody has hijacked the address or tampered with it midway. But since this has the unwanted effect of making domains harder to recall, scammers have a much easier time generating lookalike addresses or creating website clones.

For example, many popular websites use “vanity prefixes” to make their onion addresses more easily identifiable or to add some branding appeal. That means their 56-character onion link starts with something like “facebook,” “bbcnews,” or “ciadotgov.” But scammers can use a free tool like mkp224o to generate lookalike addresses with the same vanity prefix as the legitimate website, which gives people a false sense of security.

Of course, most dark web owners don’t type addresses directly into Tor Browser; they use dark web directories like the Hidden Wiki to find useful onion sites relevant to their search. Scammers will create fake search engines or link directories to point users to their fake websites, like when the Ahmia search engine discovered that a copy of its platform was directing users to 255 cloned services back in 2015.

Industry observers note that of course, it’s possible to orchestrate phishing attempts that don’t involve cloning sites at all. Researchers at Freie Universität Berlin describe a sophisticated technique where attackers serve the real website through their own reverse proxy, which lets them manipulate parts of the site or log your online activity without your awareness. In 2019, ESET even found a trojanized version of Tor Browser that replaced Bitcoin addresses on websites to direct payments to hackers. So both genuine websites and your browser itself are also vulnerable to manipulation if you download or access them from an unverified source.

In a recent development, there are a few best practices to avoid phishing attacks when using the dark web. None of them are foolproof on their own, but together, they considerably lower the risk of ending up on a fake or manipulated website.

The Tor Project has a feature called Onion-Location, which lets clear web websites advertise that they have a dark web version available for consumers who prefer more privacy. If opening a regular TLS-backed website using the Tor Browser reveals a purple “onion available” button in the address bar, you can click on it and be redirected to the official onion link associated with that site.

On the desktop version of Tor Browser, you can access an onion site using a shortened version of its URL called an Onion Name. For now, this feature only works with SecureDrop, so newsrooms can establish tip lines with addresses like mysitename.securedrop.tor.onion, which would then redirect to the 56-character original onion address. This feature is in active development, so more platforms might support it in the future.

Industry observers note that when you load up an onion site using the Tor Browser, you’ll see an onion icon on the address bar, which confirms that your connection is end-to-end encrypted. But you can also click on the onion icon to check if the site has an Extended Validation (EV) certificate, which tells you that its authenticity has been verified by a trusted certificate authority like DigiCert. While not every legitimate onion site will have an EV certificate, famous ones like Facebook tend to.

According to recent reports, on the other hand, if you see a caution sign next to the onion icon, that means the site is using a self-signed or expired certificate that isn’t guaranteed by a trusted authority. It may also imply that the site is being served over an insecure URL. This doesn’t definitely tell you it’s a phishing site, but it’s a red flag to watch out for nevertheless.

Don’t rely on search engines, link directories, Reddit threads, or Telegram channels too heavily on the dark web. Once you’re sure you’ve found the onion address for a genuine site, bookmark it so you can access it directly the next time you want to visit.

If you realized that you’ve been the victim of a phishing attempt, the first step is to close the browser window with the fake site and access the real onion address to reset any account passwords you may have accidentally divulged.

It has been revealed that also, generally try to enable two-factor authentication and PGP logins on any dark web account that supports it for added security. And if you downloaded Tor Browser from anywhere other than the official Tor Project site, uninstall it now and grab a fresh copy from the official address.

Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1291 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the company's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors.
  • BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals.
  • Build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the company's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it says on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

Build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Unveiled in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

In a recent development, the same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The tech giant grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "right now engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

Sources indicate that as reported by The Shanghai Observer and Automaton, authorities in Shanghai have arrested 13 people and seized an untold number of unauthorized model kits and figures based on pop culture properties like Final Fantasy. The cops were reportedly put on the trail by a suspect Tifa Lockheart figurine.

Industry observers note that police in Fengxian, a district of Shanghai, began receiving complaints in June. The Shanghai Observer showed pictures comparing a Play Arts Kai (Square Enix's premium figure line) Tifa with a seemingly less articulated counterpart in the same outfit. Reading through machine translation, it sounds like customers in the area bought these figures online expecting the genuine article.

According to recent reports, the leader of the operation reportedly commissioned a Guangzhou factory to produce the false Tifa and her ilk. They even sold some figures at higher prices than the genuine article, offering added accessories or features not available in the official product.

I'm of two minds about this, personally: I'm generally pro-kitbashing, selling custom figures, and using proxies in trading card games. In the face of some seriously inflated pricing from official merch lines, bootlegs can often be more enticing than the real deal, particularly if they offer features you can't get from official products⁠—the added customization options from this arrested vendor actually sound weirdly pro-consumer.

In a recent development, but it certainly appears, at least from The Shanghai Observer's reporting, that these suspect figures were being presented as the genuine article to customers. Paired with the increased price vs. official merch, and I find myself soured on the whole operation. It may seem small and silly, but as we endure the Golden Age of Scams, it's weirdly nice to see scammers face some consequences somewhere.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

Sources indicate that "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.".

So, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

This GTA VI Comparison To Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour Blew My Mind (But Fans Are Less Impressed)

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto VI came out on November 19, and literally one day after that, it was confirmed that it had hit $3.79 billion in sales.
  • In a recent development, to get into the specifics, it was reported by Rockstar Games that GTA VI has reached $3.79 billion in sales as of November 20, per The AP.
  • Recent findings suggest that looking at the Eras Tour, specifically, after its 21-month run, it racked up $2 billion in tickets sold and over 10 million people attended the concerts (its proshot was also a major box office success and can now be streamed with a Disney+ subscription).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto VI came out on November 19, and literally one day after that, it was confirmed that it had hit $3.79 billion in sales. That’s a seriously impressive number. I mean, it took Taylor Swift nearly two years to make $2 billion with her highly profitable Eras Tour. GTA did more than that in one day. However, while that is quite mind-blowing to think about, fans aren’t so impressed by this comparison.

In a recent development, to get into the specifics, it was reported by Rockstar Games that GTA VI has reached $3.79 billion in sales as of November 20, per The AP. It also stated that 32.5 million units were sold in pre-release. When People published a story on what the video game had reportedly made, it prominently noted that it had already outgrossed Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour.

Recent findings suggest that looking at the Eras Tour, specifically, after its 21-month run, it racked up $2 billion in tickets sold and over 10 million people attended the concerts (its proshot was also a major box office success and can now be streamed with a Disney+ subscription). The NYT, that’s “double the gross ticket sales of any other concert tour in history.” Also, reportedly, the tour’s average gross per night was between $14 and $17 million.

In a recent development, considering the fact that both the Eras Tour and GTA VI were highly anticipated events – Taylor Swift hadn’t toured in six years before Eras, and fans waited 13 years for the newly introduced GTA – I get why this comparison is staggering. It’s honestly wild that it took GTA one day to do more than what Taylor Swift did in a little less than two years.

However, many fans made it clear they weren’t that impressed by this comparison.

When you really think about it, comparing GTA to the Eras Tour is like comparing apples and oranges. One is a concert tour; the other is a video game. Yes, they’re both major moments of monoculture. However, that’s kind of all they have in common. So, that left people commenting things like this on People’s post about the video game outgrossing Swift’s tour:.

Something many comments pointed out was that there was a cap on how many people could attend the Eras Tour. There are only so many people you can fit in a stadium. Anyone can buy and play Grand Theft Auto VI. So, it makes sense that it could make more than the tour in such a short period of time.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It might be more fitting to compare GTA VI's release to this year’s box office, considering almost anyone can go to the movies if they want to. In one day, this video game managed to make more than the current highest-grossing film on the 2026 movie schedule, which is Spider-Man: Brand Upcoming Day (the film made more than $2 billion worldwide during its run in theaters this summer).

In a recent development, then, if we really want to compare apples to apples, Grand Theft Auto V generated $1 billion in sales during its first three days. In total, the 2013 game accounts for over 230 million of the franchise's 470 million units sold. It would seem the sixth installment is well on its way to beating its predecessor.

Recent findings suggest that anyway, getting back to GTA and The Eras Tour, overall, I agree with fans in a way, because this is a hard comparison to make. However, it’s also undeniable that the release of GTA VI and The Eras Tour are two of the biggest pop culture moments in recent history, and it is kind of wild that the video game managed to outgross the concert series in one day.

  • In a recent development, the location for an entire row of GTA 6 tanks is in the Mile Zero Air Station, situated west of the area you begin the story in, which you can reach by driving through Abismo Key and on to Southwind.
  • Industry observers note that by following the route marked on my map above you'll weave through several road barriers, as which point the soldiers will open fire on you, then turn right at the first opportunity to pass more barriers and soldiers until you spot a handy pile of dirt.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Getting a tank in GTA 6 represents the pinnacle of criminal behavior, and there's a long history of stealing Rhinos going all the way back through the series to GTA 3! These military vehicles are virtually indestructible so you're safely protected inside, and they pack a powerful enough punch with their cannon to destroy anything GTA 6 puts in front of you. You also need to get inside one to unlock the Challenging Tank Trophy or Achievement, so to help you out with that, here's how to steal a tank in GTA 6.

In a recent development, the location for an entire row of GTA 6 tanks is in the Mile Zero Air Station, situated west of the area you begin the story in, which you can reach by driving through Abismo Key and on to Southwind. You'll need a vehicle to break into the military base which will get left behind, so it's best not to use your GTA 6 personal vehicle for this job, and equipping body armor from Ammu-nation is highly recommended for added protection.

Industry observers note that by following the route marked on my map above you'll weave through several road barriers, as which point the soldiers will open fire on you, then turn right at the first opportunity to pass more barriers and soldiers until you spot a handy pile of dirt. You must use this Stunt Jump to clear the perimeter fence, though if you don't get enough height to also clear the inner fence you can smash through it to reach the runway.

Look to your left when on the miliary runway and you'll see a large building, and to the left of that are the Rhino tanks we're looking for – you can also head to the right of that building if you'd prefer to grab a GTA 6 jet instead. Once you reach the tanks, crash through the fence and then approach one before using the usual enter vehicle button to climb in through the front hatch. Note that there is various military hardware in this area, but the Rhino tanks are the ones closest to the fence you broke through.

You can then drive away in your fresh GTA 6 tank, which will shortly unlock the Challenging Tank award from the GTA 6 Trophy and Achievement list to add to your collection. Strangely, commandeering this military vehicle doesn't initially increase your GTA 6 Wanted Level beyond the existing two-stars for breaking into the base, though this soon goes to five and then six-stars when you start blasting things with your cannon.

In a recent development, don't expect to get too far in your Rhino tank, as it drives pretty slowly and you're being constantly peppered with incoming gunfire plus rockets from helicopters – which you can shoot down if you aim your barrel high enough. However, the tank will eventually run out of fuel or become so damaged that it is completely incapacitated, and as surrender is no longer an option the upcoming Wasted is unavoidable.

The Wanted Level you get won't affect your current GTA 6 criminal profile, though you can only get a six-star Wanted level in GTA 6 if you go all in on a psychotic rampage!

It really seems like Xbox isn't allowed to say GTA 6 at all

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • Recent findings suggest that as pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the substantial release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles.
  • Recent findings suggest that "Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is important.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6. Unlike indie publisher Devolver Digital, however, Xbox has cleverly avoided ever mentioning GTA 6 directly in its marketing campaigns for GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that as pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the substantial release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles. Despite that, it does not mention GTA 6 by name a single time.

Recent findings suggest that "Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is important. "We can hardly believe it's almost here, either.".

Recent findings suggest that one day prior, Xbox Wire partnered with DJ Khaled to create custom doctor's notes for players to submit to their employers to take the day off. Why would you want to take 19th November off? Because you're apparently having "a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency".

Going even further back, Xbox revealed a custom-made Series X console it called X-Bite, which is a large, sculpted alligator that swallowed a Series X console. Why? Because "this November, Xbox is heading to Florida - home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe.".

Florida, of course, is the real-world US state GTA 6's Leonida is based on, but in keeping with the theme of not referring to the game - or its made-up state - directly, the blog does not.

Industry observers note that now, Xbox has directly named GTA 6 in places, but only when, seemingly, the post is about factual information. This Xbox Wire post reiterates GTA 6's Xbox Cloud streaming availability, and this one is a look-ahead at games launching the following week on Xbox. But that's about the extent of what you can expect.

Recent findings suggest that so what's going on here? The simple guess is that PlayStation has a co-marketing deal with Rockstar, meaning no other console platform gets to use GTA 6's name in marketing. Sony is allowed to make custom, GTA 6-themed consoles, branded, limited-edition DualSense controllers and blaster the game all over the PS Blog, social media, and even change the PS App's icon colour to match the hue of GTA 6's.

This is all too similar to when, each year, various brands encourage you to buy their products to be ready for The Big Game, which is very distinct from the Super Bowl happening on the same day. Like Xbox, those brands simply don't have the rights to the real thing.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 is available now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. In Eurogamer's five-star review, Chris Tapsell wrote, "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games.
  • Sources indicate that in development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time.
  • The original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a fresh developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

Sources indicate that in development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

The original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

Raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

According to recent reports, gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the new team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The version 3.4 enhancement for Zenless Zone Zero, dubbed “The Finality of the Day,” will launch on December 2, developer miHoYo confirmed.
  • Industry observers note that the story of the Sky Island of Roscaelifer reaches its final climax, as Sunbringer, a latest Void Hunter and the first Enchainer Agent, joins the fight.
  • In Version 3.4, Roscaelifer’s main story is about to reach its climax.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The version 3.4 enhancement for Zenless Zone Zero, dubbed “The Finality of the Day,” will launch on December 2, developer miHoYo confirmed.

Here is an overview of the update, via miHoYo:.

Industry observers note that the story of the Sky Island of Roscaelifer reaches its final climax, as Sunbringer, a latest Void Hunter and the first Enchainer Agent, joins the fight. The new version also kicks off the Zenless Zone Zero × Honkai: Star Rail collaboration, introducing two crossover Agents, Robin and Kafka, along with themed events. It also brings new combat gameplay, updates to permanent game modes, and a variety of version rewards.

In Version 3.4, Roscaelifer’s main story is about to reach its climax. From the Bangboo corruption incident to High Ambitions Corp.’s invasion, the Proxies and their allies have weathered crisis after crisis together. Now, the enemy has stepped out of the shadows, and Roscaelifer faces a decisive battle for its very survival. For the first time, the three Sunbringers — Dracaene, Lindverne, and Eldreda—will fight side-by-side, joining the Proxies to take on a formidable foe and defend Roscaelifer. Upcoming characters and menacing enemies are taking the stage, while the arrival of an unexpected character leaves even more mysteries hanging over this new chapter. How will this storm change the fate of the Celestial Nexus? What trials await the Proxies and their allies? All will be revealed in “The Finality of the Day.”.

Once this version upgrade goes live, Sunbringer, leader of Roscaelifer, joins the fray as an S-Rank Genesis Flare Armorer Agent, bringing a unique offensive and defensive rhythm through a three-member synergistic combat style: Eldreda, Lindverne, and Dracaene take turns stepping in with a lance, greatsword, and shield, seamlessly balancing offense and defense. Their Armorer attacks can stack Gash on enemies, and consuming Gash triggers Maim while building up Wishfire. Once Wishfire is sufficient, Eldreda can hold Basic Attack to hurl her lance and make her entrance, following up with a synergy Chain Attack. When Decibels are sufficient, they can unleash a two-stage Ultimate that detonates all Embermark stacks on the enemy at once, triggering Emberburst for massive damage. When the upcoming version releases, Proxies can obtain Sunbringer and the S-Rank Armorer W-Engine Dragonfire Mirage via Signal Search. On top of that, the new Bangboo Sleepwalkerboo will also arrive in the Bangboo Channel, summoning Bangboo soldiers to back you up in combat and boosting Sunbringer’s damage when Sunbringer is on the squad.

According to recent reports, the two crossover Agents also bring their own distinct combat styles. Robin can keep up her Concerto performance off-field, granting teammates shields while boosting their DEF and DMG, and can extend her support effects by re-entering the field. Her Ultimate can also restore Sharpness for Armorer Agents. Meanwhile, Kafka, an S-Rank Electric Agent, builds her offense around Attribute Anomalies and Disorder DMG. While in the Hunter’s Overture state, she can choose between slashing or shooting attacks, enhancing direct DMG or speeding up Attribute Anomaly buildup, respectively. When her slashes hit an enemy afflicted with an Attribute Anomaly, she can also trigger a Lightning Surge to deal additional DMG. Robin’s brand-fresh outfit, Cosmic Beat, will also be made available. Sunbringer’s and Robin’s Signal Search channels will open on the first day of the enhancement and run throughout Version 3.4, while Kafka will arrive in the second half of the version. As for reruns, the S-Rank Physical Anomaly Agent Alice and the S-Rank Anomaly W-Engine Practiced Perfection will return in the second half of the version.

Beyond combat, Dracaene, Lindverne, and Eldreda will each have their own Trust Events, showcasing the distinct daily lives of the three Sunbringers. Once all three reach max trust level, Proxies will also unlock a special side quest to help secretly initiative their birthday party. Their new daily wear outfit, Moonlit Promenade, reveals a side of the three Sunbringers as they step into city life, letting Proxies experience up close Dracaene’s gentle sweetness, Lindverne’s playful personality, and Eldreda’s bold, free-spirited charm. The Moonlit Promenade outfit set and its matching Starlit Stroll Limited Gift will also be available. The latter includes a three-person Accompany Experience and an exclusive Idle Action, so Proxies can enjoy their everyday company on the streets of New Eridu. A dynamic wallpaper and three matching Inter-Knot avatars will also arrive with this version.

As for events, the collab event “Lost in a Theatrical Dream” between Zenless Zone Zero and Honkai: Star Rail kicks off in Version 3.4. Proxies will team up with Robin, Kafka, and their New Eridu companions to film a series, featuring stealth raids and Agent interactions. Complete the event to score rewards like the collab Bangboo Pom-Pom and Polychromes. On top of that, the new version also brings the “Opening Act: Enter the Knight” combat mode and a new “Dark Dungeon Survival” season for Enigma of the Labyrinth. Proxies can join in to earn Polychromes, a profile icon, new accessories, and more.

Zenless Zone Zero is available now for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, PC via client download, Steam, and Epic Games Store, iOS via App Store, and Android via Google Play.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The BF Bandito is one of the many cars in GTA 6 that Moses asks you to steal and bring to him for cold, hard cash. This one has a search area out in Buskin Swamp, but when you arrive it's not immediately clear where or how to steal the car.

Recent findings suggest that the owner of this white offroad racer will drive around the map marked search area in a circle, as shown in the clip above. To get him to stop, simply park your car blocking the track and stand next to it. When he reaches you, he'll slow down and call out, at which point you should press L2 to focus on him and use the "Mislead" dialogue option to ask for help.

In my version, Lucia was wearing a ski-mask and had a baseball bat, which rapidly convinced them all to run away (after a few swings), but either way, once he stops it's easy to steal the car. The baseball bat probably wasn't necessary, but hey, it's still non-lethal.

Sources indicate that as you exit the swamp, you'll get shot at and pursued by a few of his friends, but the BF Bandito is fast enough to outrun them easily. Bring it back to Moses to get $3,400ish as reward, though this may vary based on condition.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that in a first substantial revision since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have confirmed some additions coming to the community-run backend database.
  • "We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick enhancement on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.
  • Recent findings suggest that there are two main new features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in a first substantial revision since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have confirmed some additions coming to the community-run backend database. Affiliate links aimed at providing options to help folks find the cheapest price for a game and a new tab dedicated to the mods Nexus host for a game are incoming, as work on behind-the-scenes improvements continues.

"We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick enhancement on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.

Recent findings suggest that there are two main new features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon. The first is one that anyone could have seen coming, a new tab on each moddable game's page that demonstrates off some mods hosted for it on Nexus Mods and a host of modding-related data. "The new tab will help you discover mods for games you're browsing on SteamDB, making it easier to see whether a game has an active modding community and explore what it has to offer," Fomann wrote. "For now, we'll only be showing mods from Nexus Mods, as we already have access to that wealth of modding data, making it a straightforward starting point for this new feature.

Industry observers note that "We appreciate that some of you might be wondering why we're not including Steam Workshop, too. It's certainly something we'd be open to exploring as we develop the feature further, along with other modding sources. With that in mind, if you run a modding website and would be interested in having your community's mods included, we'd love to hear from you.".

That seems perfectly fine, but the other incoming feature's a bit more controversial given SteamDB's historically not been all about the money. "One thing we've seen people ask for is an easier way to find the cheapest place to buy a game, and we're now working on making that possible," Folmann wrote. "We'll be introducing affiliate links to authorised game retailers, giving you more options when looking for the best available price on a game.

"We recognise that introducing affiliate links may raise some concerns, so we want to be clear about how they'll work. First and foremost, as I mentioned, we'll only feature authorised retailers; we will not be including grey-market resellers. We've also made a deliberate decision about how prices are displayed: retailers will be ordered by the cheapest available price in your currency, not by whichever retailer offers us the highest affiliate commission. If a retailer doesn't offer pricing in your currency, we'll still show deals in other currencies provided they are available in your region.".

It has been revealed that folmann was clear in the initial announcement of the takeover that Nexus Mods' bosses would be actively looking into ways SteamDB could make more money to sustain itself, so the addition of these links isn't out of the blue either. Whether SteamDB regulars agree that they're a "lighter-touch" way of earning the site some cash without detracting from the traditional experience of using it is another matter. I'll need to see how I feel once I've actually navigated a few pages with the links in as part of looking up stuff about games, but my first instinct is that as long as the pages don't end up revolving around the links and it's still easy to get to the info you want without interacting with them, I probably won't be too put out.

Sources indicate that beyond those tweaks, Folmann mentioned "improvements to how updates are tested before they go live" and how promptly the team can react to issues have been among the less obvious work going on behind the scenes. "We're still in the early stages of what we want to achieve, and there's plenty more work we need to do and would like to work on," he wrote in closing.

Folmann and co only took over Nexus Mods in June last year, making them still relatively new custodians of both it and SteamDB.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We’d rightly criticise Sony if the PS5 had fallen to pieces during GTA 6’s launch, so let’s give the platform holder a nod of approval for navigating these past two weeks almost flawlessly.
  • Sources indicate that there were some minor scattered instances of PSN outages on Wednesday evening prior to the Rockstar title’s big launch, but these never affected everyone and the network recovered pretty fast.
  • Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, the preload process worked flawlessly as far as I’m aware.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We’d rightly criticise Sony if the PS5 had fallen to pieces during GTA 6’s launch, so let’s give the platform holder a nod of approval for navigating these past two weeks almost flawlessly.

Sources indicate that there were some minor scattered instances of PSN outages on Wednesday evening prior to the Rockstar title’s big launch, but these never affected everyone and the network recovered pretty fast. I think we can give that a pass.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, the preload process worked flawlessly as far as I’m aware. I haven’t really seen any widespread reporting of people being unable to download the game in advance of its release.

Given its size and the sheer number of people wanting to play – remember, 32.5 million copies were sold across all consoles prior to release – that’s a humongous strain on Sony’s servers, which is predicted to have accounted for approximately 75% of all purchases.

Obviously GTA 6 is a single player-only game, so that certainly put less stress on the PSN as a whole, and the fresh GTA Online’s eventual launch will be an even bigger test – but for now, the PS5 has held up remarkably well.

I’m not saying we should get out the champagne – this is the experience consumers quite rightly expect Sony to deliver.

But this was still a huge, unprecedented test for PlayStation’s infrastructure – and it’s fair to say it navigated it almost flawlessly. In my opinion, that deserves acknowledging at least.

As A Theater Kid, I Have So Many Feelings About Elsinore

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (749 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that actor Andrew Scott is synonymous with playing Hot Priest in Fleabag (streaming with an Amazon Prime subscription), but he's a versatile star of the screen and stage.
  • I'm a proud theater kid, one who is still acting and producing to this day in the community theater space.
  • It has been revealed that while Club Kid is my favorite movie of the year (so far), Elsinore is another LGBTQ+ story that I feel privileged to have seen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that actor Andrew Scott is synonymous with playing Hot Priest in Fleabag (streaming with an Amazon Prime subscription), but he's a versatile star of the screen and stage. Those two worlds combine in the new LGBTQ+ movie Elsinore, directed by Simone Stone. The biographical drama film tells the story of late actor Ian Charleson, who performed the title role of Hamlet at the National Theatre while secretly struggling with AIDS in the midst of the AIDS crisis. The movie is endlessly powerful, and I have so many thoughts as someone who comes from the theatre.

I'm a proud theater kid, one who is still acting and producing to this day in the community theater space. While I loved Andrew Scott's stunning performance in Elsinore and the way it honored Charleson and the countless queer folks that we lost to the AIDS crisis, I was also taken by how accurately the new film portrayed what it's like to work in theater... warts and all.

It has been revealed that while Club Kid is my favorite movie of the year (so far), Elsinore is another LGBTQ+ story that I feel privileged to have seen. The movie tells the real-life story of Ian Charleson struggling with AIDS while also preparing to play the behemoth role of Hamlet at the National Theatre. It's a truly gut-wrenching story, told expertly through the film's 111-minute runtime. Throughout the movie, I was shook by how seen I felt by the way it portrayed working on a theater production.

To start, there was the almost neurotic way that Ian is shown preparing to play the titular character Hamlet. We see him working long hours in the sparse rehearsal room, where experimentation and heeding notes from director Richard Eyre transformed his performance from a piece of marble into a detailed statue. While stage actors make this look easy, there is way more work than casual audiences might grasp from their seat in the house.

Then there was the process of line memorization. Ian is shown drilling lines pretty much non-stop throughout Elsinore, including when he's getting treatments and even while recovering after being hospitalized. This rings so true to me; if I'm in a dialogue-heavy play, I function in the same way. For instance, when I played Prior Walter in Tony Kushner's Angels in America, I couldn't stop drilling my lines. That includes testing myself with flashcards, as well as repeating my monologues every time I was in the shower and/or driving in the car.

Much like Ian in Elsinore, getting those lines ingrained in my head allows for more freedom and expression during performances, rather than searching for what comes next in my head.

Then there's the sense of community that's shown in the new movie. While Ian spends most of the movie hiding his diagnosis, he eventually tells them the truth before opening night. He expected judgment, but his colleagues rapidly accept him and offer support for his performance. This feels very true to the experience of being in the theater; weird chosen families often form with each production. I've seen ensembles rally around people struggling with grief, miscarriages, election results and more.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Sources indicate that overall, it really felt like Elsinore was created by folks who knew and love what it means to work in the theater. Obviously this isn't the point of the movie per se, but it's one of many reasons why I thought it was so incredible.

Recent findings suggest that elsinore is in theaters now as part of the 2026 movie release list. Word to the wise: bring your tissues.

After working in administrative theater for a year in New York, he started as the Weekend Editor at CinemaBlend. He's since been able to work himself up to reviews, phoners, and press junkets-- and is now able to appear on camera with some of his favorite actors... just not as he would have predicted as a kid. He's particularly proud of covering horror franchises like Scream and Halloween, as well as movie musicals like West Side Story. Favorite interviews include Steven Spielberg, Spike Lee, Jamie Lee Curtis, and more.

Industry News: 10 Demonstrates Like 'The Traitors' You Should Watch Next

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, what started as De Verraders way back in 2021 has become a global reality phenomenon: Peacock in the U.S.
  • A reality show with a complex history as relates to The Traitors, the premise being so similar that it may well have served as an inspiration.
  • In a recent development, if there were a prize for dramatic title (and set design), you could do a lot worse than this one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, what started as De Verraders way back in 2021 has become a global reality phenomenon: Peacock in the U.S. hosts the American version with the sartorially supreme Alan Cumming, and also the earlier UK take as well as iterations from Australia, Canada, and New Zealand—but there are spin-offs in France, India, Germany, Ireland, Turkey, and more. Basically, throw a dart at a map and you're likely to hit a country with its own take on The Traitors. And yet! The addictive nature of reality TV means that we can't really ever get enough. In that spirit, here's more backbiting reality TV, and a couple of dramas that offer up similarly duplicitous thrills.

A reality show with a complex history as relates to The Traitors, the premise being so similar that it may well have served as an inspiration. Here, players participate in collaborative missions in order to build a prize fund. But it's not all fun and games: There's a secret double agent among the group (the mole, obviously) whose sole task is to undermine the ability of the rest of the group to earn money. Eliminations are done via quiz: The group is grilled on the information they've collected about the mole, and whoever knows the least gets the boot. Originally airing in the aughts, Netflix brought it back for a couple of seasons more recently, with the potential for more to come. Stream the most recent seasons of The Mole on Netflix.

In a recent development, if there were a prize for dramatic title (and set design), you could do a lot worse than this one. In this South Korean reality show, 12 celebrity contestants are challenged to build a prize pot through strategy games. Sometimes they're collaborative, sometimes entirely competitive, and sometimes a blend, but prizes come in the form of "Pieces" that can be won or lost (and that eventually combine to create their own final puzzle). Anyone who finds themselves without a single Piece is out. Pieces can be spent to buy advantages, and also traded, so the show turns on players forming alliances in order to build the prize pot and survive as long as possible. Stream The Devil's Blueprint on Netflix.

Here, a bunch of strangers are holed up in an apartment building, cut off from the outside world—and each other. Players can only interact via a custom app, and, thus, can portray themselves however they want, whether that means being 100% genuine (unlikely!) or creating a whole newly introduced persona. Players judge the competition based on their interactions, determining the "Influencers" who will get to decide on the eliminations. The show ran for seven seasons on Netflix, and is moving to Hulu for the forthcoming eighth. Stream The Circle on Hulu.

You show up at a fancy hotel, and someone hands you a suitcase containing one million dollars. It's yours to keep—as long as you can keep it a secret. In this one, all the contestants get a suitcase, and only one contains the money. Much as with The Traitors, the goal is to figure out who's keeping the secret, with challenges designed to help flush that person out. If the truth is discovered via a vote, that former millionaire is ousted and the money is concealed in another suitcase until the final contestants are given the opportunity to swap bags with someone who they think has the money. Easy come, easy go, I guess. Stream Million Dollar Secret on Netflix.

I'm a little more into the normies on Traitors myself, but there's no question that a big part of the appeal (for most seasons) is watching reality-show celebs go at it with cash on the line. So it is with House of Villains, a Big Brother-style competition with Joel McHale as ringmaster. The core premise is pretty simple: villains (Richard Hatch, Tom Sandoval, Jonny Fairplay, one-time Trump bestie Omarosa Newman, etc.) compete in challenges for rewards and for safety from the inevitable banishment. It's all mostly an excuse to watch some of TV's biggest personalities go for each other's jugulars. Stream House of Villains on Peacock.

Sources indicate that this is not a reality show, but rather a drama about a reality show that may well slake your thirst for treachery while offering up consequences a bit more dramatic than the bruised egos and hurt feelings of The Traitors. Here, eight strangers are selected to compete in a game in which they're locked together in a building and sequestered on different floors each night. They earn money for each minute they last in the game, but all their provisions must be purchased with money they've won, at an extreme markup. At first, the contestants pool their resources so that everyone gets more money—until they learn that people on higher floors are getting more. Then things get nasty Stream The 8 Show on Netflix.

According to recent reports, this one plays a bit like The Traitors in reverse: A $250,000 prize pot is, right off the bat, allocated to all 11 contestants who get to hang out in a luxurious villa. So the game isn't about winning money so much as it is about how much you'll keep and how much you're willing to share. Eliminations offer the opportunity to remove those who the others don't want to share with—though contestants don't have to actually ever vote anyone out. They can just keep their portion of the money and hang out, something that obviously does not happen. Challenges along the way force contestants to reveal embarrassing and sometimes ugly truths about themselves that may well put them on the outs with the others. There's only one season at present, though there's potential for more. Stream The Trust on Netflix.

Blending the Big Brother-esque social aspects of Traitors with Survivor's love of the great outdoors, this one drops four teams of four into the Alaskan wilderness (moving to Panama for season three). The contestants are all, by inclination, loners, but the game has only one core rule: Only a team (of at least two) can win, so while the game has the typical reality show eliminations, these wilderness enthusiasts must work together in order to take the money. In the same way that The Traitors creates a tension between competition and cooperation via its communal prize pot, Outlast sees its contestants forced to maintain relationships whether they like it or not. Stream Outlast on Netflix.

It has been revealed that the tasks on Traitors aren't typically the most thrilling part of the show, which makes this James Bond-branded competition a solid match if you want more complicated and better developed challenges. In this one, nine teams of two visit exotic locations in each episode and compete in spy-themed activities with the ultimate goal of winning £1 million by making it to the end. It leaves out the bits where people sit around a castle strategizing, but it includes, like Traitors, a dapper Scotsman not afraid to camp it up—in this case, Brian Cox, serving as the spymaster who directs the teams in their missions. Stream 007: Road to a Million on Prime Video.

Squid Game: The Challenge would probably be a more reasonable choice for this list—given that it's a proper reality show and not a blood-chilling thriller. But I'm sticking with the original drama here since, as perfectly entertaining as that spin-off is, it feels like it misses the point. In the original (surprise smash hit) drama, 454 needy contestants are recruited for a newly introduced reality competition in which they're tasked to play rather simple children's games—with deadly consequences that are cheered on by the wealthy financiers who are willing to pay good money to watch both the poors go at each other, as people turn on each other to survive and to win the rather shockingly large prize. A bit like The Traitors if all of Alan's murder schtick were literally true. Stream Squid Game on Netflix.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 debuts on console today. It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining. And yet, staff at Rockstar Games are apparently worrying about being laid off, as development winds down and investors start to bicker about Line Going Up Even More.

In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

Sources indicate that the animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section. Following some personal reflections on his time at the studio, he calls on other Rockstar devs to get behind the union, describing it as both "a huge step forward" for a manufacturer that has previously faced allegations of "crunch culture", and a win for UK game developers at large. "What happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more," Uriarte writes.

The vote at Rockstar North will run till 26th November, and could give rise to a union spanning over 1600 developers, according to umbrella organisation the Independent Workers of Great Britain. If that comes to pass, it would make the Rockstar union the largest recognised videogame developer union in the UK.

It comes as the organization and a group of fired workers await the result of an employment tribunal battle over alleged "union-busting". Rockstar has accused the workers in question of "gross misconduct" and a breach of confidentiality by means of a union Discord server. Amongst other things, the legal brawl has revealed that Rockstar had a mole on that server for two and a half years, prior to the firings.

As for the prospect of further job losses, after GTA 6 goes on sale, Uriarte cites a wave of mass layoffs across the industry that has affected the creators of even commercially successful games like Battlefield 6 and Netflix's FIFA World Cup.

According to recent reports, "After the substantial day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds," he writes. "Studios across the industry have been slashing huge portions of their workforces, with an estimated 24,000 roles axed globally over the last two years. It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

The obvious context here is that GTA 6 has been a massively expensive production, with a development team headcount in the thousands. While one could accuse Uriarte of fear-mongering, I do find it hard to believe that executives at parent organization Take-Two aren't weighing up some timely "down-sizing" right now. In general, videogame companies have a long tradition of axing the books once a game has been shipped, despite arguments that keeping experienced teams intact often pays off. In Rockstar's case, however, it's also worth bearing in mind that the GTA 6 rolling out this week is only part of the package. There's also the hazy prospect of the next incarnation of GTA Online, which – going by GTA 5 sales – will be a money spinner for many years, and will require a sizeable staff to maintain. Oh, and of course there's the PC version.

Echoing many peers, Uriarte also argues in his piece that it's key to unionise now in order to negotiate proper protection against generative AI cost-cutting initiatives. "The rapid emergence of AI is transforming how studios work and raising fundamental questions about the future of our industry," he continues. "Across the sector, the skills that workers spend years developing risk being devalued as their creative work is replaced by AI.

"Rockstar has noted it is committed to preserving jobs and it has been clear that our games will continue to be made by people," Urirarte concedes. "But with recognition we’d have a seat at the table to manage this industry-wide transition together.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developer Digital Dreams, and publisher and developer Firenut Games have delayed psychological horror game Baptiste from its previously planned fall 2026 release window to March 25, 2027. It will be available for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Switch 2, and PC via Steam.

Here is an overview of the game, via Firenut Games:.

Sources indicate that at the center of Baptiste‘s narrative-driven adventure is Tom, a child who frees an eerie doll from its display case and is thrust into a fear-soaked journey. Through his eyes, Baptiste explores how tragedy and loss can fracture a family’s reality, and how a child struggles to cope with the emotional scars of devastating events.

It has been revealed that baptiste draws inspiration from classic horror tales like the allegedly possessed doll Annabelle and R.L. Stine’s Goosebumps story Night of the Living Dummy, as well as fan-favorite psychological horror games such as P.T., Layers of Fear, and the Outlast series. The game combines exploration and environmental storytelling as players explore an ominous mansion, piece together clues, and solve puzzles to uncover its dark secrets and the story behind the game’s titular living doll.

In a recent development, following a family tragedy, Sara and her son, Tom, seek a fresh start at Jagged Shore Cliff, but it rapidly unravels into a fresh nightmare. In their new and mysterious home, a dusty cabinet holds Baptiste, an unsettling doll accompanied by an ominous warning: “Never release this from its glass prison.” What ought to have been a shelter becomes the scene of a nightmare that defies all logic, putting their sanity and desire to survive to the test.

Rather than rely on jump scares, Baptiste‘s take on the psychological horror genre combines atmospheric tension and emotional depth, exploring how tragedy and loss can fracture a family’s reality, particularly through the lens of a child attempting to cope with intensely traumatic events. It also examines the descent into madness, blurring the lines between what is real and what is a nightmare, reflecting the fragile state of the mind under extreme emotional distress to tell a story of human vulnerability.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent.
  • But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear.
  • Sources indicate that "After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent. GTA 6 is already one of the highest-rated games ever - Eurogamer awarded it five stars in our GTA 6 review - and it's expected to be among the most successful, best-selling games ever.

But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear. Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar North, wrote about their concern for their job and those of their colleagues in an article on The Guardian.

Sources indicate that "After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. "It notes a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

According to recent reports, uriarte's piece comes as Rockstar staff's efforts to establish a union reach a critical point. A tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

Rockstar's UK studios are currently voting on recognising an official Rockstar workers union. Uriarte is in support of it and has urged colleagues to vote in favour of it. Results of that vote are expected today.

"Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that," Uriarte pointed out.

"As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry - one in which workers' voices are taken into account more.".

Across its 12 offices around the world, Rockstar's headcount grew to 4,711 during GTA 6's development - double its size when it released Red Dead Redemption 2.

As popular and profitable as Rockstar's games are, the company has initiated layoffs in the past after shipping a major project. While there's no way of knowing whether the same is going to happen for GTA 6, the justifiable concerns - given the current state of the industry - are there. According to the ASGC Games Industry Layoffs Tracker, more than 12,000 developers have lost their jobs this year so far, up from more than 9,000 people last year.
